title: Multi-centric, prospective natural history study on the frequency of infections before and after cellular therapy (INFE-CT) in patients with hematologic malignancies in comparison to the general population
summary: This study investigates how often haematological patients get infections before and after cell therapy compared to the general population. It also examines whether certain types of treatment - such as stem cell transplants or modern immunotherapies - influence the risk of infection. Important immune parameters are also taken into account. The results should help to develop future infection prevention measures.
conditions: Condition after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation with current immunosuppression
Condition after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation without current immunosuppression

interventions.name:
Patients with hematological malignancy and indication for cell therapy defined as either (I) autologous stem cell transplantation or (II) CAR T-cell therapy or (III) bispecific antibody treatment 

Observation period from Q1 2026 to Q1 2029
a control cohort from the general population (IV)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Stated willingness to comply with all study procedures and availability for the duration of the study. Ability of subject to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.
2.	Age ≥ 18 years
3.	Subject diagnosed with hematological cancer and planned to initiate one of the following treatments:
I: autologous stem cell transplantation after high-dose chemotherapy
II: CAR T-cell therapy 
III: bispecific antibody treatment
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Subjects with a diagnosis of congenital disorder of the immune system.
2.	Subjects with solid tumors as indication for cellular therapy. History of solid cancer, in remission at initiation of study does not represent an exclusion criterion.  
3.	Previous CAR-T cell therapy or previous therapy with bispecific antibody.
